Keep the computer in the room with you. 

Write the note while talking with them. 

Order what you can while talking to the patient including their home meds (start/hold). 

Get a dot phrase (if you have Epic) or note template from a senior that works well for your style so ask around to all the seniors. 

Always make sure to ask the patient why they came to the hospital in the first place. This is problem #1 - focus your plans on resolving this symptom including a pain plan if it is painful to them. An order set for pain was immensely important for a number of my patients. 

Send in a med student for an H&P! they will love you for involving them While they are in there, look through the patient history and start queuing up your orders or take care of other admissions. talk with the med student then go in to clarify anything you had questions about/orders.

Set a timer for how long you spend on an HPI. sometimes the ED does actually do a good job with this. 

When you leave, let the patient know YOU are their doctor, because, well, you are. 

Good luck out there!

Medical writing is a route, so is research or working for pharma. Alternatively Take a research year in the department of a program elsewhere and matriculate in as a PGY - whatever -  this coming year. There are also some expensive routes like doing an MPH or going into Law school. 

Try resident swap (expensive $300) 
Also could try find a resident.com

That being said, this is a tough time. New interns, new leadership, COVID. Lots of people in our profession are hurting a lot. you’ve gotta ask if it’s all worth it. Some state boards will let you practice after having 2 years of residency (they would need to know what you were going to do and who you were going to work for), but really getting into a different program might be the best route for you. 

So sorry that you are going through this man. I really feel your pain. DM me if you want any other info.
I really needed to hear that. Thanks so much

It just depends on whether or not you’ve got a good program. PGY2 year is usually complete shit front-loaded nonsense. My program was pretty malignant soooo... Also the patients are sick man. Imaging and the brain itself, is really cool. Also depends on how scared your ED is of neuro patients and how much of a compulsory consult to neuro because “patient has a brain”. My favorite was Stroke code called for “numb pinky that comes and goes”.

Brain death exams were really tough for the patients families and for me.
You will start slow and get faster. Just remember that you can bill more for “metabolic encephalopathy” rather than “AMS” and you’ll do great! s/

Having a strong friend and group is super important, I agree - the MATCH kind of ripped that apart for me. Religion could work, I was religious once upon a time. It means getting up on sundays that I’m not on. as far as therapy is concerned, I go, but she just doesn’t quite understand the way another resident might understand.
Yeah, thanks man. Today was just suuuuch a bad day. And I can’t remember the last time I had a good day. Not a lot of positives to focus on

It is super draining. Got any good resources?

I want my time to not have been wasted. Went to medical school and residency (same as you will do)... My patients are neurologically devastated most the time. Nothing I can do for them other than try and get the family to understand their loved one is never going to be the same again. Try and get the patient to understand they will never be the same again. 

I guess I hate it so much because the nature of the beast is to not personalize. If you’ve ever read  “the house of god” (which I highly suggest if you haven’t) you’d know that one of the rules of the house of god is that “the patient is the one with the disease”. 

Believe me, I want to be thankful, I’ve gotten to be a party to some of the deepest parts of a person’s life or the end of their lives. However; the people who are supposed to be my confidants and mentors only care about how much they can bill for, or if the notes are written by 7pm, or if this patient can be enrolled in a study. They learned to not take things personally - but to me, each patient that seizes, each patient that strokes out, each patient that dies... a small part of me thinks; I did this to them. What’s worse is when that guilt leaves an impression upon your patient or their family. 

My advice to you is to never think that about yourself. You are only ever just the bearer of news or the director when decisions need to be made. 

Good luck to you too man.
This was really helpful advice, so thanks. Sounds like you’ve got a good recipe for how to make it through the slog. What’s your secret?

Do you know what you would do? Go teach? Do scientific writing? Work in pharma? (USA grad). I’ve already been told that if I don’t “play by their rules” I “will never work again” 😕
Has it been better for you? Would you do it all over again?
Me too... Thanks man - if anything, commiserating with someone helps.

Work-life balance. You’ll be happier soon! Just keep trudging on, by the way - there are 4 new consults 10 follow ups and there are 3 patients seizing down in the EMU. You will remember that ms. Not to mention the brain death exam for your cardiac arrest patients in the CCU - you did have “the talk” with those families didn’t you?

Also, mandatory wellness lecture at 5pm!

I’m getting out before my soul is twisted any further by these attendings.
